clusters.name: Cluster B
items: Uncomfortable when not center of attention (DSM p.757)
Inappropriately sexually seductive or provocative behavior (DSM p.757)
Rapidly shifting and shallow expression of emotions (DSM p.757)
Consistently uses physical appearance to draw attention (DSM p.757)
Excessively impressionistic speech lacking detail (DSM p.757)
Considers relationships more intimate than they actually are (DSM p.757)

criteria.thresholds: ≥5 out of 8 criteria, starting by early adulthood (DSM p.757); ≥1 year continuous duration if under age 18 (DSM p.736)

epidemiology.sex_ratio: 1:1 M:F in epidemiological studies; clinically diagnosed significantly more in females (DSM p.759)
epidemiology.prognosis: Symptoms and dramatic outward expression tend to lessen with age (Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders)

etiology.genetic: High Novelty Seeking (NS) and High Reward Dependence (RD) temperament traits (Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders)
etiology.neurobiology: Impaired Top-Down cortical inhibition (OFC, VMPFC, ACC) over hyperactive Bottom-Up limbic/ventral striatal drives; mesolimbic dopamine and serotonin dysregulation (StahlNeuro p.540, p.577)
etiology.environmental: Psychodynamic defenses of Repression and Dissociation against underlying rejection fears (Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders); developmental role experimentation in adolescents (Dulcan p.200)

items: Borderline Personality Disorder: BPD includes self-harm/NSSI, chronic emptiness, identity diffusion, and intense fears of abandonment not seen in HPD (DSM p.759)
Narcissistic Personality Disorder: NPD seeks admiration for superiority/grandiosity, whereas HPD is willing to appear weak or vulnerable to get attention (DSM p.760)
Antisocial Personality Disorder: ASPD manipulates for material gain, power, or money (with Conduct Disorder history), whereas HPD manipulates to gain nurturance and affection (DSM p.759-760)
Dependent Personality Disorder: DPD exhibits submissive, docile, and self-effacing behavior, unlike the theatrical and demandingly active HPD (DSM p.760)
Somatic Symptom / Conversion Disorder: Can be diagnosed concurrently if somatic symptoms cause significant distress/impairment (DSM p.760)
key_numbers: ≥5/8 DSM criteria required for diagnosis (DSM p.757)
≥1 year continuous duration required if diagnosed under age 18 (DSM p.736)

first_line: Psychodynamic / Psychoanalytically oriented psychotherapy focused on clarification of inner feelings and processing repression/dissociation (Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders)
second_line: SSRIs/SNRIs for depressive symptoms, emotional reactivity, and somatic complaints (Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders, StahlKids p.208)
Low-dose SGA (e.g. Aripiprazole, Risperidone, Quetiapine) for stress-induced micro-psychosis or illusions (Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders, StahlNeuro p.159)
key_side_effects: Benzodiazepines carry high risk of dependence, abuse, and behavioral disinhibition in Cluster B disorders (Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders)
Activation, motor restlessness, and suicidal ideation monitoring with SSRIs in children/adolescents (StahlKids p.323)
treatment.monitoring: Monitor target symptoms, suicidal gestures/threats, diagnostic fluidity/morphing in adolescents, and avoid benzodiazepine misuse (StahlKids p.313, Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders)

high_yield: HPD core feature: pervasive pattern of excessive emotionality and attention seeking requiring ≥5 of 8 criteria starting by early adulthood (DSM p.757)
Pediatric criteria constraint: must be present continuously for at least 1 year if diagnosing under age 18 (DSM p.736)
Differentiating HPD from BPD: HPD lacks chronic emptiness, identity diffusion, NSSI, and self-destructive behavior typical of BPD (DSM p.759)
Differentiating HPD from NPD: NPD demands admiration for superiority/grandiosity; HPD is willing to appear weak or dependent to gain attention (DSM p.760)
Differentiating HPD from ASPD: ASPD manipulates for material gain, power, or money; HPD manipulates to gain nurturance and affection (DSM p.759-760)
Speech style: Impressionistic speech style that is theatrical and dramatic but excessively lacking in detail or factual support (DSM p.757)
Psychodynamic defenses: Primary defenses are Repression and Dissociation (Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders)

Treatment of choice: Psychodynamic psychotherapy aiming at clarification of authentic inner feelings (Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders); avoid benzodiazepines due to abuse risk (Synopsis ch.19 Personality Disorders)
